article_title: Developmental dyscalculia is related to visuo-spatial memory and inhibition impairment
citation: Szucs Denes, Devine Amy, Soltesz Fruzsina, Nobes Alison, Gabriel Florence. (2013). Developmental dyscalculia is related to visuo-spatial memory and inhibition impairment. Cortex, 49(10). https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cortex.2013.06.007
title: Inhibition impairment as disruption of central executive visuo-spatial working memory in developmental dyscalculia
description: The article proposes an explanatory account in which the WM and inhibition impairments detected in DD are related: "the inhibition impairment may have led to impaired visuo-spatial WM performance". On this view, DD reflects specific impairment of visuo-spatial STM and of the inhibitory processes crucial to visuo-spatial central executive WM function, and IPS differences in DD may relate to interference resolution rather than magnitude representation function.
requirements: Requires measuring STM and WM capacity separately in the verbal and visual modalities, as the article argues modality-specific WM systems dissociate
constraints: The account is offered as a hypothesis; the article states the inhibition impairment may have led to impaired visuo-spatial WM performance rather than demonstrating this causally
target_learners: primary school children with developmental dyscalculia
examples: The study measured inhibition via congruency effects in four Stroop-type experiments and a Stop-signal task, and visuo-spatial WM via the AWMA Odd One Out subtest
key_sources: Szucs Denes, Devine Amy, Soltesz Fruzsina, Nobes Alison, Gabriel Florence. (2013). Developmental dyscalculia is related to visuo-spatial memory and inhibition impairment. Cortex, 49(10). https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cortex.2013.06.007

article_title: Inhibitory Control and Information Processing in ADHD: Comparing the Dual Task and Performance Adjustment Hypotheses
citation: Fosco, W. D., Kofler, M. J., Alderson, R. M., Tarle, S. J., Raiker, J. S., & Sarver, D. E. (2019). Inhibitory Control and Information Processing in ADHD: Comparing the Dual Task and Performance Adjustment Hypotheses. Journal of Abnormal Child Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10802-018-0504-9
title: Drift diffusion model decomposition of stop-signal slowing: performance adjustment versus dual-task hypotheses
description: The article uses the drift diffusion model (DDM), a well-validated stochastic accumulator model, to decompose task performance into parameters with distinct cognitive interpretations: drift rate (processing speed), boundary separation (response caution), and non-decision time (encoding/motor speed). Within this framework, the dual-task hypothesis predicts slower drift rate and non-decision time with no boundary-separation change, while the performance adjustment hypothesis predicts increased boundary separation with stable drift rate and non-decision time. The study's results matched the performance adjustment pattern. As the article states, "Boundary separation (a) refers to the quantity of information considered before a decision is executed and reflects one's degree of response caution".
requirements: Requires both RT and accuracy data integrated by the model, estimated per participant per task (Kolmogorov-Smirnov algorithm via fast-dm software)
constraints: The article notes non-decision time conflates stimulus encoding and motor response speed, which are not separable in the diffusion model
The study could not determine whether performance adjustments are proactive or reactive
target_learners: children ages 8-13 with and without ADHD
target_learning_goals: understanding neurocognitive mechanisms of inhibitory control and response strategy adjustment
examples: The study estimated drift rate, boundary separation, and non-decision time separately for the No-Tone and Stop-Signal tasks for each child, with acceptable model fit for all participants (all ps > .05)
key_sources: Fosco, W. D., Kofler, M. J., Alderson, R. M., Tarle, S. J., Raiker, J. S., & Sarver, D. E. (2019). Inhibitory Control and Information Processing in ADHD: Comparing the Dual Task and Performance Adjustment Hypotheses. Journal of Abnormal Child Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10802-018-0504-9

citation: Liane Kaufmann, Michael von Aster, Silke M. Göbel, Josef Marksteiner, and Elise Klein. (2020). Developmental Dyscalculia in Adults: Current Issues and Open Questions for Future Research. Lernen und Lernstörungen, 9(2), 126–137. https://doi.org/10.1024/2235-0977/a000294
title: Tentative working model differentiating number-related and number-unspecific deficiencies in adult DD
description: The review proposes a tentative working model (Figure 3) suggesting a differentiation between number-related and number-unspecific (domain-general) deficiencies characterizing DD in adulthood at both cognitive and brain levels. Number-related core deficiencies include automatic activation of number magnitude knowledge, enumeration, arithmetic fact retrieval, and arithmetic conceptual knowledge; number-unspecific dysfunctions include attentional processes, working memory, and response latencies. The model is offered as a building block for future research to formulate hypotheses, develop diagnostic marker tasks, and design interventions.
requirements: Requires validation by clinical and longitudinal developmental evidence per the review
constraints: The review states the current evidence is based on only a handful of studies and findings should be interpreted with caution
target_learning_goals: attention and working memory in numerical contexts
examples: The review's Discussion section enumerates the specific number-related deficits reported across studies and the domain-general dysfunctions, organizing them into the two-category model depicted in Figure 3
key_sources: Liane Kaufmann, Michael von Aster, Silke M. Göbel, Josef Marksteiner, and Elise Klein. (2020). Developmental Dyscalculia in Adults: Current Issues and Open Questions for Future Research. Lernen und Lernstörungen, 9(2), 126–137. https://doi.org/10.1024/2235-0977/a000294

article_title: Mindfulness training enhances face working memory: evidence from the drift-diffusion model
citation: Kou, H., Luo, W., Li, X. et al. (2025). Mindfulness training enhances face working memory: evidence from the drift-diffusion model. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-025-00389-0
title: Drift-diffusion model decomposition of working-memory decision processes
description: The drift-diffusion model (DDM) is a perceptual decision-making framework that separates components hidden in raw accuracy and reaction-time data by modeling stochastic evidence accumulation from a starting point to a decision boundary. The article fits four parameters: drift rate (v, average evidence accumulation speed), decision boundary (a, response caution), bias (z, starting point), and nondecision time (t). The article states that "The DDM provides a robust framework for decomposing decision processes into distinct components," and uses it here to identify which component of working-memory performance mindfulness training changes.
requirements: Response-time and accuracy data from each participant and condition to fit the Bayesian hierarchical model (dockerHDDM, 10000 samples, 5000 burn-ins)
constraints: The article notes behavioral indicators "include components beyond cognition," which is the motivation for decomposition; parameter interpretation depends on task structure (the DMTS task here)
target_learning_goals: decomposing working-memory decision processes into processing efficiency, response caution, bias, and nondecision components
examples: The study fitted v, a, z, and t per condition and subject, finding training effects on v but stable a and z.
key_sources: Kou, H., Luo, W., Li, X. et al. (2025). Mindfulness training enhances face working memory: evidence from the drift-diffusion model. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-025-00389-0

article_title: The Implementation of Interactive Multimedia Learning Materials in Teaching Listening Skills
citation: Andi Tenri Ampa. (2015). The Implementation of Interactive Multimedia Learning Materials in Teaching Listening Skills. English Language Teaching, 8(12). http://dx.doi.org/10.5539/elt.v8n12p56
title: DDD-E four-phase development of multimedia learning materials
description: The article describes developing the multimedia listening materials through "four phases: Decide, Design, Develop, Evaluate (DDD-E) proposed by Ivers and Baron (2010)". This is a reusable development cycle for producing interactive learning materials: decisions about the materials, their design, their development, and evaluation of the resulting product. In this study the cycle produced expert-validated materials that were then summatively evaluated for effectiveness in a quasi-experiment.
requirements: Expert validation and student try-out of the product before implementation
examples: The article's materials were developed via DDD-E and then evaluated against Plomp and Nieveen's quality points
key_sources: Andi Tenri Ampa. (2015). The Implementation of Interactive Multimedia Learning Materials in Teaching Listening Skills. English Language Teaching, 8(12). http://dx.doi.org/10.5539/elt.v8n12p56

article_title: Teaching Semantic Prosody of English Verbs through the DDL Approach and Its Effect on Learners' Vocabulary Choice Appropriateness in a Persian EFL Context
citation: Mansoory, N. & Jafarpour, M. (2014). Teaching Semantic Prosody of English Verbs through the DDL Approach and its Effect on Learners' Vocabulary Choice Appropriateness in a Persian EFL Context. Advances in Language and Literary Studies, 5(2). https://doi.org/10.7575/aiac.alls.v.5n.2p.149
title: Teach semantic prosody of near-synonym verb sets through data-driven learning with corpus concordancing rather than dictionaries alone
description: The article's central pedagogical recommendation is that semantic prosody be taught by having learners themselves examine keyword-in-context concordance lines from corpora such as the Brown corpus and BNC, inducing the prosodic behavior of whole synonym sets. The study concludes "the DDL approach is a better way for finding out the prosodic behavior of English words" than traditional dictionary- or intuition-based instruction. Teachers provide training, guidance, and feedback while learners work with concordancers individually or in groups.
requirements: Access to corpora and a concordancer, with initial and ongoing training in their use
A teacher who advises, helps, and gives feedback on learners' concordance analyses
constraints: A few students found the approach confusing and difficult
The study tested only verb near-synonyms in receptive mode with male learners in one institute
target_learners: Adolescent EFL learners (ages 16-18) with at least 3000 English words
target_learning_goals: Awareness of semantic prosody of verbs
examples: Treatment students examined concordance lines for the word USE and its synonyms, reporting that EMPLOY had a positive, RESORT TO a negative, and others a neutral semantic prosody
key_sources: Mansoory, N. & Jafarpour, M. (2014). Teaching Semantic Prosody of English Verbs through the DDL Approach and its Effect on Learners' Vocabulary Choice Appropriateness in a Persian EFL Context. Advances in Language and Literary Studies, 5(2). https://doi.org/10.7575/aiac.alls.v.5n.2p.149
